result:
The way sunlight filters through the leaves of an old oak tree in my backyard reminds me of how fleeting yet persistent beauty is. It’s not just the light—it’s the way it dances on the ground in shifting patterns, as if time itself is playing a silent game of hide-and-seek. Sometimes I sit under that tree for long stretches, watching the world move around me while I stay still, as if I’m trying to absorb the quiet lessons nature offers.

There’s a comfort in stillness, even when the rest of life feels like a whirlwind. The tree doesn’t rush. It grows, it sheds, it stands firm through seasons—sometimes violent, sometimes gentle. I wonder if it ever feels impatient, or if its roots dig deeper the louder the chaos above gets. I think not. The tree doesn’t know urgency. It simply *is*.

That’s how I want to be, sometimes. Not in a detached way, but in a grounded one. To let go of the need to always be doing, always be reacting. To trust that some things can unfold without my constant interference. Maybe that’s what peace looks like—not the absence of noise, but the ability to exist within it without losing your center.

I don’t always succeed. Most days, I’m the squirrel darting from branch to branch, frantic and scattered. But on my better days, I’m the oak. Rooted. Watching. Waiting. Learning.

And sometimes, that’s enough.
